s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive headaches and visual field defect with a history of intracerebral hemorrhage and a left occipital mass
salient_findings: Left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage on noncontrast head CT
Left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage on contrast-enhanced brain MRI
key_facts: 36-year-old Asian man
4-month history of worsening headaches
Complete right homonymous hemianopia
History of left occipital intracerebral hematoma of unknown cause 2 years earlier
Normal vital signs
Neurologic testing confirmed visual field defect without other focal deficits
Noncontrast head CT showed left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage
Contrast-enhanced brain MRI revealed left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage
Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields
Immunohistochemical studies showed strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive headaches and visual field defect with a history of intracerebral hemorrhage and a left occipital mass
salient_findings: Left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage on noncontrast head CT
Left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage on contrast-enhanced brain MRI
key_facts: 36-year-old Asian man
4-month history of worsening headaches
Complete right homonymous hemianopia
History of left occipital intracerebral hematoma of unknown cause 2 years earlier
Normal vital signs
Neurologic testing confirmed visual field defect without other focal deficits
Noncontrast head CT showed left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage
Contrast-enhanced brain MRI revealed left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage
Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields, and immunohistochemical studies showed strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1

shortlist.label: Meningeal sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination and immunohistochemical studies suggest a malignant tumor with sarcomatous features, and meningeal sarcoma is a plausible diagnosis given the tumor's location and characteristics

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: The tumor's vascular nature and the presence of branching ectatic vasculature are consistent with hemangiopericytoma, a rare vascular tumor

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: The tumor's histopathological features, including spindle cells and branching ectatic vasculature, are also consistent with epithelioid hemangioendothelioma, a rare vascular tumor

shortlist.label: Gliosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: The biphasic pattern of glial and mesenchymal differentiation suggested by the histopathological examination could be consistent with gliosarcoma, although the immunohistochemical profile is not typical for this diagnosis

raw.rationale: Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and high mitotic activity, and immunohistochemical studies showed strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1, which are consistent with angiosarcoma.

rejected.label: Meningeal sarcoma
rejected.why: While meningeal sarcoma could be considered, the specific immunohistochemical profile and histopathological features are more indicative of angiosarcoma.

rejected.label: Hemangiopericytoma
rejected.why: Hemangiopericytoma typically shows a more uniform staining pattern for CD34, which was negative in this case.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma usually presents with a distinct epithelioid morphology and a different immunohistochemical profile.

rejected.label: Gliosarcoma
rejected.why: Gliosarcoma would typically show a biphasic pattern of glial and mesenchymal differentiation, which was not the primary feature in this case.
